sources.content:
Search fundamentals
A short reference for the Asteria Chat interface review.
Uniform-cost search selects the frontier node with the lowest path cost g(n).
A* adds a heuristic estimate h(n) to prioritize promising paths.
The evaluation function is f(n) = g(n) + h(n).
Search fundamentals | 1

The role of the heuristic
In A* search, g(n) is the path cost from the start to node n.
h(n) estimates the remaining cost from node n to a goal.
A* selects the frontier node with the lowest estimated total cost f(n).
If h(n) is zero everywhere, f(n) equals g(n), so A* behaves like
uniform-cost search under the same graph-search assumptions.
An admissible heuristic never overestimates the actual remaining cost.
This is a reference document for UI verification, not a learning assessment.
Search fundamentals | 2

answer: A* combines the path cost so far, g(n), with the estimated remaining cost, h(n): f(n) = g(n) + h(n). It selects the frontier node with the lowest f(n). [1]
